headline: Buoyancy is the upward force that fluids exert—it's why some things float and others sink
universal_truth: What supports you matters as much as what you carry; the right environment lifts you up
fun_facts: Steel ships float because they're shaped to displace more water than their weight—it's about density, not just weight
The Dead Sea is so salty that you float effortlessly on the surface
Helium balloons float in air because helium is less dense than the surrounding atmosphere
discussion_questions: What environments help you 'float' or stay afloat?
How do you create more support in your life?

hook.title: Welcome
hook.script: A massive steel ship floats. A tiny pebble sinks. Why? It's not about weight—it's about density and displacement. Fluids push back on objects, creating buoyancy. The right conditions make heavy things float.

options.text: I want to learn something new
options.response: Perfect. Curiosity is the first step to understanding. Let's explore this together.
That curiosity is exactly what we need. Let's dive in and discover something amazing.

cliff.title: The Question
cliff.script: Floating isn't magic—it's physics. Objects displace fluid, and that fluid pushes back. What determines whether something floats?

options.text: An object floats if it's less dense than the fluid it's in—or if it's shaped to displace enough fluid that the buoyant force exceeds its weight
options.response: Yes. Float or sink depends on the relationship between the object and its environment. The same object can float in one fluid and sink in another. Context matters.

options.text: Light things float, heavy things sink
options.response: Weight matters, but so does density and shape—heavy ships float while light coins sink...

q1.title: Displacement
q1.script: When you put something in water, it pushes water aside—displacement. The displaced water pushes back with a force equal to its weight. If that upward push exceeds the object's weight, it floats.

options.text: This confirms what I already knew
options.response: Great foundation! Now let's build on that knowledge with something you might not expect...
Perfect starting point! This insight will connect to even more surprising facts ahead.

q2.title: Density Comparison
q2.script: Density is weight per volume. If your density is less than water, you float. More, you sink. Oil floats on water. Mercury sinks. The comparison—not the absolute—determines buoyancy.
q2.prompt: How does this connect to what you already know?

options.response: Exactly. These connections are how knowledge becomes understanding.

options.text: I need to think about this more
options.response: That's a good instinct. Deep understanding takes time. The next fact will help clarify.

q3.title: Environmental Support
q3.script: In life, your environment provides buoyancy too. Supportive relationships lift you. Toxic environments drag you down. The same person thrives or sinks depending on context. Choose environments that help you float.
q3.prompt: What surprises you most about this?

options.text: I never thought about it this way
options.response: That shift in perspective is exactly the point. New angles reveal new truths.
That's learning in action. When understanding shifts, you're really getting it.

wisdom.title: Today's Wisdom
wisdom.script: Here's today's wisdom: What supports you matters as much as what you carry. The right environment lifts you up. Seek contexts where you float.
wisdom.prompt: What resonates most with you today?

options.response: That central truth will stay with you. Let it guide your thinking.
Application is where knowledge becomes wisdom. That's the real learning.

outro.title: See You Tomorrow
outro.script: That's Day 226. Tomorrow, we'll explore how things stay in the air—flight. Until then, consider what environment helps you stay afloat.
outro.prompt: Before you go—what will you take from today?

options.response: Reflection deepens learning. Let these ideas simmer in your mind.
Teaching others is the best way to learn. You've already begun the ripple.

growTrack.title: Buoyancy Audit - What Lifts You?
growTrack.activity: What environments, relationships, or contexts help you 'float'—make life feel easier, more supported, more possible? What drags you down? Can you spend more time in high-buoyancy environments? Support systems aren't weakness—they're physics.
